The Franks were a Germanic people who rose from the Rhine frontier to become the dominant power in Western Europe, establishing kingdoms that evolved into the Merovingian and Carolingian empires. They originated along the Rhine as Roman foederati before expanding into Gaul after the empire's collapse. Under Clovis I, they unified Frankish territories and defeated the last Roman forces in Gaul, establishing Frankish dominance while converting to Catholic Christianity—a move that gained them the support of Roman provincial populations. The Merovingian dynasty ruled for three centuries, maintaining Roman administrative structures while gradually consolidating Germanic warrior culture. The Carolingian dynasty that followed, particularly under Charlemagne, transformed the Franks into an empire that revived imperial authority and patronized learning, creating a remarkable cultural renaissance. They developed a sophisticated feudal system and maintained written law codes that preserved both Roman and Germanic legal traditions. Unlike the Ostrogoths, Visigoths, and Vandals whose kingdoms crumbled, the Frankish kingdom endured and evolved into the medieval kingdoms of France and Germany. They also pioneered military innovations, including the use of heavy cavalry and the stirrup, tactics that would dominate medieval warfare for centuries to come. Of all the Germanic peoples, the Franks alone built a lasting political and cultural legacy that shaped medieval Europe.
